label: The Protestant Family Tree
title: Where today's evangelical churches came from
intro: Four streams came out of the sixteenth-century Reformation. Baptists, Methodists, the Holiness movement and Pentecostals grew out of them later. Each line ends with one example body today; there are many others.
image_subtitle: Four sixteenth-century streams and the movements that grew out of them, with one example body today.
image_subtitle_narrow: Four Reformation streams and the movements that grew out of them.
caption: Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican and Anabaptist churches all date to the 1500s. Baptists came out of English Separatism in 1609, Methodism out of the Church of England in the 1700s, the Holiness movement out of Methodism, and Pentecostalism out of the Holiness movement.
image_source: Sources: each body's own history page; Christian History Institute; Christianity Today; Baptist News Global

differ: Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican and Anabaptist churches all began in the Reformation of the 1500s.
Baptists came out of English Separatism; how much they owe the Anabaptists is still debated, so that link is dashed.
Methodism began as a renewal movement inside the Church of England before forming its own churches.
The Holiness movement grew out of Methodism, and Pentecostalism grew out of the Holiness movement.
note: Dates are each body's own or a church history publisher's. The examples are one of many in each family.
